stem: On what date was the Lancaster House Agreement signed?

options.content: 21 December 1979
options.rationale: Correct: the agreement was signed at the end of the conference.

options.content: 18 April 1980
options.rationale: This is Independence Day.

options.content: 11 November 1965
options.rationale: This is the date of UDI.

options.content: 22 December 1987
options.rationale: This is the date of the Unity Accord.

explanation: The Lancaster House conference ran from September to December 1979, and the agreement was signed on 21 December 1979.

stem: How many of the 100 House of Assembly seats did the Lancaster House constitution reserve for whites?

options.rationale: Correct: 20 seats for seven years.
The number reserved was larger than this.
The number reserved was smaller than this.
This would have been half of the House.

explanation: Twenty of the 100 seats were reserved for white voters for seven years.

stem: What did the **willing-buyer willing-seller** clause mean for land?

options.content: Any person could take unused land without paying for it
options.rationale: The clause protected owners and required payment.

options.content: Government could buy land only from owners who agreed to sell
options.rationale: Correct: owners could not be forced to sell during the protected period.

options.content: Land could be sold only to foreign buyers
options.rationale: The clause did not restrict buyers in this way.

options.content: All land became state land at independence
options.rationale: Private ownership was protected.

explanation: For ten years, land could be acquired only when the owner was willing to sell, with compensation, which slowed redistribution.

stem: In which year did an **executive presidency** replace the offices of ceremonial President and Prime Minister?

options.rationale: In 1980 there was a ceremonial President and a Prime Minister.
This was the year of the rejected draft constitution.
This is when the new Constitution was adopted.
Correct: the executive presidency dates from 1987.

explanation: A constitutional amendment created the executive presidency from 1987.

stem: Which reason for replacing the Lancaster House constitution is about **how often it was changed**?

options.content: It was negotiated in London under British chairmanship
options.rationale: This is about where and by whom it was made.

options.content: It had been amended many times and became a patchwork
options.rationale: Correct: frequent amendments weakened confidence in it.

options.content: Its property clauses slowed land redistribution
options.rationale: This is about land.

options.content: Citizens wanted their own languages and values reflected
options.rationale: This is about national identity.

explanation: Many amendments made the constitution hard to follow and suggested it was changed to suit those in power.
hints: Look for the reason about amendments.

stem: What happened in the referendum of **February 2000**?

options.content: Voters approved the Lancaster House constitution
options.rationale: That constitution was never put to a referendum.

options.content: Voters approved the constitution now in force
options.rationale: That was the referendum of 16 March 2013.

options.content: Voters rejected a draft constitution
options.rationale: Correct: the draft was rejected.

options.content: Voters elected a new President
options.rationale: A referendum decides a proposal, not a candidate.

explanation: The draft of 2000 was rejected; the 2013 draft was approved on 16 March 2013.
hints: Two referendums: one draft rejected, one approved.

stem: Why did the Lancaster House constitution include reserved seats and protected property?

options.content: because the liberation movements had asked for them at the conference
options.rationale: They were concessions made by the liberation movements, not their demands.

options.content: to make land reform faster after 1980
options.rationale: The property clauses slowed land reform.

options.content: to reassure the white minority and make a ceasefire possible
options.rationale: Correct: these were compromises to end the war.

options.content: because Zimbabweans voted for them in a referendum
options.rationale: There was no referendum on the 1979 constitution.

explanation: The constitution was a compromise: reserved seats and property protection reassured the white minority so that a settlement could be reached.
hints: Who needed to be reassured for the war to end?

stem: Which point **best** supports the view that a home-grown constitution has greater legitimacy?

options.content: It is longer and has more chapters than the old constitution
options.rationale: Length does not create legitimacy.

options.content: It is written by experienced foreign lawyers
options.rationale: That would make it less home-grown.

options.content: It can be changed easily by any government
options.rationale: Easy change weakens rather than strengthens legitimacy.

options.content: Citizens take part in making it and approve it in a referendum
options.rationale: Correct: participation and approval give authority.

explanation: A constitution that citizens helped to make and approved in a referendum is widely accepted as their own.
hints: Legitimacy comes from the consent of the people.

A second different provision

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It reserved 20 of the 100 House of Assembly seats for whites for seven years, it allowed land to be acquired only on a willing-buyer willing-seller basis for ten years, and it contained a Declaration of Rights.

stem: Explain **two** reasons why many Zimbabweans wanted to replace the Lancaster House constitution.

points.description: Identifies: it was negotiated abroad / was a ceasefire compromise
Develops: made in London under British chairmanship to end a war, so it did not reflect the long-term wishes of Zimbabweans
Identifies: it was amended many times / land clauses / demands for stronger rights and wider participation
Develops: frequent amendments by governments of the day weakened confidence; citizens wanted a constitution they had made themselves

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It was negotiated in London under British chairmanship as a compromise to end the war, so many felt it did not reflect what Zimbabweans wanted for the long term. It was also amended many times by governments of the day, which weakened public confidence, and citizens wanted a constitution they had helped to make.

explanation: One mark for each reason and one for its development.
hints: Where and why was it made? What happened to it after 1980?

stem: Suggest **two** ways citizens can help to make sure the Constitution is respected and not changed lightly, and explain each.

points.description: Suggests learning about the Constitution / civic education in schools and communities
Explains that people who know their rights can recognise and challenge violations
Suggests taking part in public hearings on amendment bills / voting in referendums / approaching the courts
Explains that wide participation means changes reflect the people's wishes and unlawful acts can be corrected

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Citizens can learn about the Constitution through civic education in schools, churches and communities, so they know their rights and can recognise when they are violated. They can also attend public hearings on amendment bills and vote in referendums, so that any change reflects the wishes of the people rather than of a few.

explanation: One mark for each suggestion and one for its explanation.

> Our constitution was written in a foreign city to stop a war. It has been changed many times by those in power, often without asking us. It did bring us independence and majority rule, but we, the people, should now write our own.

Read Source A and answer the questions.

points.description: It was written abroad to stop a war
It was changed many times by those in power without consulting citizens

stem: This question is about the Lancaster House constitution.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe **three** main features of the Lancaster House constitution.

points.description: Reserved seats: 20 of 100 House of Assembly seats for whites
for seven years (abolished in 1987)
Property protected: land acquired only on a willing-buyer willing-seller basis
with compensation, for ten years
A Declaration of Rights / a two-house Parliament / ceremonial President and Prime Minister
explained (e.g. protecting civil and political rights; Westminster-style system)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: First, it reserved 20 of the 100 House of Assembly seats for white voters for seven years; they were abolished in 1987. Second, it protected property, so land could be acquired only on a willing-buyer willing-seller basis with compensation for ten years. Third, it had a Declaration of Rights that protected civil and political rights such as freedom of expression.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: "The Lancaster House constitution served Zimbabwe well." How far do you agree?

points.description: For: it ended the war, brought independence and majority rule; it protected rights and gave stability
Against: foreign-made compromise; reserved seats; land clauses slowed redistribution
Against: many amendments, executive power concentrated; demands for reform and a home-grown constitution
Supported judgement

levels.descriptor: Developed explanation of several relevant points or arguments, supported by accurate, specific knowledge and examples, considering more than one side and reaching a supported judgement that answers the question.
Developed explanation of some factors or arguments with relevant supporting detail; a judgement is attempted but is only partly supported, or the other side is thin.
Some explanation of one or two relevant factors, or several points described with limited explanation; little or no judgement.
Simple, general or narrative statements with limited relevance to the question; little explanation.

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
The Lancaster House constitution did serve Zimbabwe in important ways. It made a ceasefire possible, brought independence and majority rule in 1980, and contained a Declaration of Rights. It also gave the new state a working system of government.

However, it was a foreign-made compromise. The reserved seats gave a small minority a guaranteed voice, and the willing-buyer willing-seller clause slowed land redistribution in the 1980s. After 1980 it was amended many times, and many citizens and organisations argued that it no longer reflected their wishes, which led to the call for a home-grown constitution.

I partly agree. It served well as a bridge from war to independence, but it was not suited to be the long-term supreme law of a sovereign nation.

explanation: A practice evaluative item on the strengths and weaknesses of the Lancaster House constitution.
hints: In (b), separate its short-term achievements from its long-term weaknesses.
